inlines.text: 这项 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究旨在通过考察用户信任的驱动因素、回答质量、理解程度和日常健康行为，为健康 AI 体验的负责任设计提供参考。

blocks.text: Apple 今日宣布在美国启动 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究。这是一项虚拟研究，并配有相关 app，旨在加深人们对用户如何与对话式健康 AI 工具互动的理解。1 该研究通过考察用户信任的驱动因素、回答质量、理解程度和日常健康行为，力求为 Apple 及整个行业的健康 AI 体验负责任设计提供参考。

inlines.text: Apple 今日宣布在美国启动 Apple 健康 AI 使用研究。这是一项虚拟研究，并配有相关 app，旨在加深人们对用户如何与对话式健康 AI 工具互动的理解。1 该研究通过考察用户信任的驱动因素、回答质量、理解程度和日常健康行为，力求为 Apple 及整个行业的健康 AI 体验负责任设计提供参考。

blocks.text: “在 Apple，我们相信负责任的创新始于科学严谨性和临床依据。健康是非常私人的事，开展一项专门的研究，是理解人们在日常生活中如何接触、理解并评估健康 AI 最周全的方式，”Apple 健康与健身副总裁 Sumbul Desai 医学博士表示。“这项研究的洞见将有助于推动更广泛的科学讨论，并确保随着技术演进，我们持续打造值得信赖的工具，真正支持人们在健康旅程中的每一个阶段。”

blocks.text: 该研究与 OpenEvidence 合作开展。OpenEvidence 是一个领先的临床 AI 平台，被医疗专业人士广泛使用，其回答基于来自《新英格兰医学杂志》《美国医学会杂志》和《自然》等权威来源的医学信息生成。这项研究将 OpenEvidence 开发的、有医学依据的 AI 技术与 Apple 设计的研究体验相结合。参与者可以在研究 app 中提出日常健康问题，以通俗易懂的语言了解复杂的医学信息，并查看为每条回答提供依据的、经过同行评审的关联临床引文。参与者还可以选择共享 HealthKit 数据类型，例如静息心率、活动、睡眠或化验结果，以探索个人数据整合如何影响相关性和理解程度。由大语言模型驱动的消费级健康技术有时可能给出不完整或不清楚的回答，因此研究对于向用户更清晰地呈现健康信息至关重要。该研究还将探索健康 AI 如何可能帮助参与者更好地为与自己的医生进行临床就诊做准备。

blocks.text: “患者和临床医生都在转向 AI，但他们使用的工具却是在彼此割裂的领域里开发和测试的，”加州大学旧金山分校（UCSF）医学教授兼内科系主任 Robert M. Wachter 医学博士说。“当患者和医生使用同一套可信工具的对应版本时，患者能带着充分准备前来就诊，对话质量随之提升，后续步骤也能顺畅衔接。把这些工具连接起来，并严谨地研究哪些做法真正有效，我们才能走到那一步。”

blocks.text: 这项研究从一开始就把隐私保护、透明度和临床安全护栏纳入设计，研究数据不会用于训练 AI 模型。参与者可以自主决定是否分享任何 HealthKit 指标或调查问卷的回答；Apple 也已采取安全措施，保护其保存的研究数据以及参与者信息的机密性。研究 App 设有安全护栏，用于识别某些令人担忧的问题，并在需要时建议参与者向医疗服务提供者或其他资源寻求帮助。

inlines.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study, conducted in collaboration with OpenEvidence, will evaluate trust, comprehension, and real-world health AI engagement

blocks.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences by examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions.

inlines.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences by examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions.

blocks.text: Apple today announced the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States, a virtual research study and associated app designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools.1 By examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions, the study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for Apple and the industry.

inlines.text: Apple today announced the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States, a virtual research study and associated app designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools.1 By examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions, the study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for Apple and the industry.

blocks.text: “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” said Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness. “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

inlines.text: “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” said Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness. “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

blocks.text: The study is conducted in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a leading clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals that generates answers using medical information from established sources such as The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. The study brings together medically grounded AI technology developed by OpenEvidence with an Apple-designed research experience. Participants will be able to ask the study app everyday health questions; explore complex medical information communicated with approachable language; and see linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations that ground each response. Participants can also choose to share HealthKit data types — such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results — to explore how personal data integration impacts relevance and understanding. Consumer health technologies powered by LLMs may at times offer responses that are incomplete or unclear, which is why research is critical to presenting health information to users with greater clarity. The study will also explore how health AI can potentially help participants better prepare for clinical visits with their own doctors.

Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine. “When patients and doctors draw on versions of the same trustworthy tools, patients arrive prepared, conversations improve, and next steps happen seamlessly. Connecting these tools, and rigorously studying what works, is how we’ll get there.”

blocks.text: The study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models. Participants retain control over whether to share any HealthKit metrics or survey responses, and Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains, as well as the confidentiality of participants’ information. The study app features safety guardrails that are intended to detect certain concerning questions and suggest that a participant follow up with a provider or other resources if needed.

blocks.text: Study Details and Availability

inlines.text: Study Details and Availability

blocks.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to up to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older across the United States. To join, participants must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later. Download the study app to learn more about the study and choose to enroll.
